description: We're a team working on the health monitoring software for astronauts challenge from this year's NASA space app challenge. We're looking for a Developer.
summary: AEGIS is an offline, AI-powered astronaut health-monitoring system that learns individual health baselines across seven physiological and behavioral indicators. It detects multi-signal anomalies, generates explainable, confidence-based alerts, and adapts medical guidance and emergency escalation to communication delays, blackouts, and crew medical availability.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

AEGIS is an offline astronaut health monitor for missions where Earth is minutes away or out of contact. It tracks seven signals (heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep, mood, activity), learns each astronaut's own baseline, and alerts only when two or more signals shift together.

HOW IT WORKS

Each alert shows its confidence and explains which signals moved and by how much. Guidance adapts to Earth delay, blackouts, and medical officer status. The astronaut decides: acknowledge, dismiss, or escalate. Escalations queue until the link delivers them. All analysis runs locally and offline.

IMPACT

It helps crews act on their health when Earth cannot answer in time, with explainable early warnings instead of raw numbers. It supports NASA Human Research Roadmap gap Medical-701.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, with a service worker for offline use and Node.js scripts for data and tests. Hosted on GitHub Pages. AI tools: Antigravity (code), Claude (research and planning).

CREATIVITY

It detects patterns across signals instead of single readings, and its guidance changes with the communication delay.

FACTORS

In-flight astronaut data is not public, so all data is simulated and labeled fictional. We used transparent rules so every alert is explainable. It is decision support only, not a medical device.
